title: Chinese Soft Power in Africa, with Maria Repnikova and Daria Impiombato
gist: MERICS podcast episode with Maria Repnikova and Daria Impiombato on Chinese soft power in Africa: Beijing's goals, methods and relative success versus the US and Europe. The page contains only the episode description.

insights.claim: A country's power lies not only in military might but also in how well it promotes its values and visions abroad, framing soft power as a strategic dimension of competition.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Influence competition in Africa shapes access to markets and resources.
insights.quote: The power of countries lies not only in their military might, but also in how well they can promote their values and visions abroad.

insights.claim: China is actively pursuing soft power in Africa, and its success is being assessed in comparison to the US and Europe.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: China-West competition for African influence affects positioning of infrastructure and resource deals.

insights.claim: Maria Repnikova's work 'Competing for Soft Power: China's image-making in Africa' underpins the discussion.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Reference reading for China-Africa influence dynamics.
